A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OTiS research work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original OTiS classification, regression and forecasting results, alongside scaling experiments, component ablations and domain-embedding analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds TUEV experiments, sine-wave studies, frozen-feature evaluations and further ablations.

M1.justification: The core architecture, tokeniser, dual masking and losses remain. v2 adds a frozen-encoder classification procedure using cosine similarity to labelled training-class centroids (Appendix F), plus linear-probing and variate-embedding-only adaptation options. These extend inference and adaptation within the existing model.

E1.justification: The eight-domain pre-training corpus and original 15 benchmark tasks remain. Coverage expands to TUEV EEG event-type classification and synthetic sine-wave representation and forecasting scenarios, including variations in fundamental signal properties and transfer to unseen frequencies.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds TimesNet to classification and iTransformer to cardiac regression. The new TUEV comparison evaluates ST-Transformer, CNN-Transformer, FFCL, SPaRCNet, ContraWR, BIOT and LaBraM (Table 12). The original forecasting comparator set remains.

E3.justification: v2 introduces frozen-feature, linear-probing, embedding-only adaptation and additional controlled training protocols, with balanced accuracy, Cohen’s kappa and weighted F1 for TUEV. Previously reported hyperparameters also change: ETTh1-Base’s learning rate changes from 1.0 to 0.03, for example (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 10), and Gesture-Base settings are revised. The EEG alignment description changes from 2D scalp alignment to 3D regression. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a no-pre-training control, masking-mixture sensitivity, EEG-only versus multi-domain pre-training, and random versus learned variate-embedding comparisons. It also adds sine-wave diagnostics, Weather embedding analysis and frozen-versus-fine-tuned representation/error analyses. Existing scaling and EEG/ECG embedding analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five fine-tuning seeds and show standard-deviation bands in the scaling study. The new TUEV table and masking-mixture plots continue the five-seed uncertainty-reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Original Table 2 and Table 3 scores are retained, while numerous baseline, frozen-feature, adaptation and ablation results are added. Examples include 95.18% Epilepsy accuracy using frozen OTiS with pre-trained variate embeddings, and TUEV balanced accuracy of 0.5743 for OTiS-Base versus 0.6616 for LaBraM under their reported settings. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements to the original scores.

T1.justification: Equation (2) revises the mathematical definition of masked decoder tokens: v1 uses the mask embedding alone, whereas v2 adds temporal and domain-specific variate embeddings. The principal loss equations remain unchanged, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The core contributions and claim of leading performance on 10 of 15 benchmarks remain. The conclusion additionally claims acquisition of shared frequency, amplitude, offset and phase knowledge through disentangling domain-specific information, extending v1’s claims about meaningful representations and inter-variate relationships.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of sinusoidal geometry, temporal transfer and physical relationships among Weather variables. Appendix F explains classification gaps through class overlap and embedding choice. Appendix G.2 qualifies applicability: adding other-domain data helps when domain data are scarce, while extensive specialist pre-training, exemplified by LaBraM, can achieve stronger results.

D1.justification: New Table 5 documents baseline architectures, pre-training corpora and adaptation methods; appendices explain centroid construction and which parameters remain frozen. Fine-tuning hyperparameter disclosures are revised, and Table 1 loses its disk-size column. OTiS architecture specifications, hardware, computational costs and code/weight access information remain.

R1.justification: The main related-work argument remains. v2 adds iTransformer, EEG comparison and dataset references, and physiological references supporting expanded embedding interpretations. Appendix G.2 develops positioning against EEG specialists. The Turgut 2023-to-2025 citation change identifies an updated publication of existing work.

P1.justification: The abstract, benchmarking narrative and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and tokeniser explanations are expanded. Dataset descriptions and detailed domain-signature analysis move into expanded appendices. The appendix structure adds dedicated zero-shot and ablation sections, moving forecast visualisation from Appendix F to H.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns, Figures 1–2 are redrawn, benchmark tables expand, and Figure 5 changes orientation and includes another control. New figures display sine-wave studies, Weather similarities, representations and masking sensitivity. Existing EEG alignment and forecast visualisations move from Figures 3 and 9 to Figures 8 and 15.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central pre-training argument by adding previously missing training-from-scratch and EEG-only controls, frozen-feature transfer evaluations and targeted signal-property studies. Better comparator documentation and acknowledgment of LaBraM’s advantage clarify applicability. The 'zero-shot' label needs qualification because Appendix F uses labelled training examples to construct class centroids, but the added controls and explanatory evidence provide a substantial net quality improvement.
